hypothesis: Keeping the iteration-3 configuration (h_px=1.5, scratch_min_contrast=0.07, scratch_min_length_px=140) and raising boundary_sensitivity from 1.0 to 1.5 will improve weak_harsh median_aspect_ratio_bias from -0.140 to >= -0.10 and bring worst_family_tolerance_ratio from 0.935 to <= 0.85. The mechanism would be fewer faint noise ridges cutting laths across their length, so the 'fragment' share of shape_population in the harsh families should fall. Guards: clean-family AR bias stays within +0.05, the 'merged' share in the clean families rises by <= 0.05, and direction/S tolerance ratios move by <= 0.02. If weak_harsh AR bias moves by < 0.03 while the fragment share stays high, noise ridges are not the cause, and the cuts most likely come from the detected-and-inpainted scratch strips themselves.
rationale:
Iteration 3 left two rival explanations for the -0.14 AR bias in weak_harsh. Missed scratches were ruled out: both weak_harsh images already have about 95% crossing recall, yet their bias is the worst of all families. Watershed over-splitting (h_px) was ruled out in iteration 2.

The two explanations left are:
(a) noise-induced ridge responses that the Otsu-based Sato threshold accepts as cross-cutting boundaries in the noisy 'harsh' images;
(b) the inpainted scratch strips acting as cut lines.

boundary_sensitivity acts after scratch inpainting and only on the ridge threshold. One change to it therefore tests (a) cleanly, without disturbing scratch detection, which sigma would also do. Every other parameter is held at the iteration-3 values so that run is the baseline.

The evaluator now reports shape_population (fragment / merged / gb_alpha) and matched_aspect_ratio_ratio. These say directly whether the AR bias comes from fragments, as expected, rather than from the per-flake measurement, and whether a higher threshold starts merging side-by-side laths. That merging is the main risk, and the reason the clean-family guards exist.

How the outcome will be read:
- Positive result: the fix lies in ridge thresholding or denoising.
- Null result: no parameter of the existing method can remove a complete cut through a lath. merge_saddle_ratio requires a non-zero neck, and bridge_gaps_px only closes along the laths. The method would then need a new scratch-aware merge step that rejoins collinear fragments across an inpainted scratch strip (orientation difference < 5 deg, lateral offset < half a lath width).

n=2 per family, so I will read per-image AR bias and not over-interpret family changes below about 0.1. Confidence that the AR prediction holds: about 40%.

Still open and not addressed by this run:
- Parallel-scratch recall of about 0.05 needs a new global Hough/RANSAC line step.
- The false scratch on moderate_clean_2 remains.
- The pooled flake_recall reporting bug should be checked.
- The Ti-6Al-4V rotation-consistency test exists via --dataset Ti64 and should be run once a candidate configuration is settled, since the real-data half of the question is still entirely untested.
